name: Lodders 2003: CI chondrite abundances and 50% condensation temperatures at 1e-4 bar

source.located: Lodders K. (2003) ApJ 591, 1220-1247, doi:10.1086/375492 (no arXiv copy; the title search on alphaXiv resolved to an unrelated paper)

Pages read: p.1220 (abstract, sec.1), p.1222 (Table 1), p.1225 (Table 3, CI chondrite group means H..Ag), p.1236 (sec.3 pressure choice), p.1238 (sec.3.1-3.2, Table 7), pp.1239-1240 (Table 8, 50% T_C, solar-system composition, complete), pp.1241-1243 (Table 9, secs 3.3.1-3.3.8).

published_statement: p.1236: 'The condensation temperatures and the 50% condensation temperatures are calculated for all elements at a total pressure of 10^-4 bar. This pressure was chosen because it is characteristic for the total pressure near 1 AU in the solar nebula (see Fegley 2000).' Table 8: 'Equilibrium Condensation Temperatures for a Solar-System Composition Gas ... Note. At 10^-4 bar total pressure. Solar system abundances from Table 2.' p.1238-1239: 'the 50% condensation temperature ... At this temperature, half of an element is in the gas and the other half is sequestered into condensates.' Table 3: 'Elemental Abundances in CI Chondrites', CI group weighted mean, ppm (e.g. P 920 +- 100, N 2940 +- 20, As 1.73 +- 0.06).
published_hypotheses: H1 total pressure fixed at 1e-4 bar, 'characteristic for the total pressure near 1 AU in the solar nebula' (p.1236)
H2 gas of solar-system (protosolar, Table 2) composition for Table 8; Table 9 is the separate photospheric set, ~10 K lower (p.1238)
H3 full chemical equilibrium: 'condensates remain in equilibrium with the gas as temperature drops'; stated NOT to apply to giant-planet, brown-dwarf or cool stellar atmospheres (p.1238)

H4 trace elements condense into solid solution in chosen host phases, selected from meteorite mineral analyses, with activity coefficients from earlier studies (p.1239); 50% T_C of trace elements depend on host availability, not on their own abundance
H5 thermodynamic data as available in 2003 (CONDOR code, ~2000 gases, 1600 condensates); halogen and Hg values flagged by the author as 'among the more uncertain' (pp.1242-1243)
H6 pressure dependence stated: metal condensation T decreases with decreasing total pressure; troilite T independent of P below 1e-2 bar; Te, Pb change host between 1e-4 and 1e-6 bar (p.1243)
H7 CI abundances: weighted means over Alais, Ivuna, Orgueil, Revelstoke, Tonk analyses available by 2003, parenthesised outliers excluded (Table 3)

YES, for stockgate's Finding F label. N overtakes P as the CI binder when CI N < 2400 ppm (tree P), < 2123 (L03 P) or < 2282 (LBP25 P). With every LBP25 row substituted, the CI chondrite binds on N at factor 13.07 (914.91 kg) and is labelled VOLATILITY-LIMITED instead of ABUNDANCE-LIMITED (computed). The datum is contested: its 1 sigma spans the crossover. D25's verdict (primitive NOT-FOUND, radius REFUSED) does not move.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. In 2003 Lodders lacked the post-2003 CI analyses (ICP-MS and isotope dilution on mg samples, Barrat 2012, Braukmueller 2018, King 2020, Palme & Zipfel 2022), the Ryugu and Bennu return samples, revised halogen thermodynamics, and 3D NLTE photospheric abundances. EVIDENCE THAT THE MISSING DATA MOVE THINGS: (a) CI N fell from 2940 to 1965 +- 970 ppm, enough in this tree to flip the CI chondrite's binder from P to N and its stockgate label to VOLATILITY-LIMITED. The new value is quality D with a 1 sigma that spans the crossover, so it is contested, not settled. (b) Cl and Br T50 fell by 530 and 123 K. EVIDENCE THAT THEY DO NOT: (c) P and the rock-forming elements move by 44 K or less, and every stockgate regime label is unchanged under the 2024 values. (d) CI P rose only from 920 to 989 ppm, which moves the feedstock figure by +5% against L03 (-5% against the tree's 1040); the 21.9 dex Proxima-b margin is untouched. (e) The 1e-4 bar hypothesis was a stated model choice in 2003 and is still one. Data did not overturn it; the author now says it more explicitly. Net: no datum Lodders lacked refutes the 2003 result. The volatility-ordering use stands. One tree-level label (the CI binder) is sensitive to a datum that has since moved and is contested.
grade_evidence: The two halves grade differently. CONDENSATION TEMPERATURES: READ at source, and the tree reproduces Table 8 in 61 of 63 entries (H and He are appearance T_C mislabelled as 50%, a discrepancy). The 1e-4 bar hypothesis is carried exactly (formation.py:501, stockgate.py:284). D25's refusal is consistent with the source's own statement that T_c depend on pressure (p.1243) and with LFME 2024. The 2024 revision at the same pressure changes no regime label. This half, and D25's verdict (primitive NOT-FOUND, snow-line radius REFUSED), STAND. CI CHONDRITE: stockgate's CHONDRITE table (stockgate.py:395) is attributed to L03 but is not L03 Table 3 (7 of 39 within 0.5%; P 1040 against 920; As x10.7). That is a discrepancy, not a refutation. Under L03's own P the tree's 749.08 kg becomes 846.79 kg, which changes no verdict. The CI chondrite's stockgate label (binds on refractory P, ABUNDANCE-LIMITED; stockgate.py:166-181, which formation's PRIMITIVE conjunct rests on at formation.py:271) moves with CI N. N crosses over below ~2100 to 2400 ppm; LBP 2025 gives 1965 +- 970 ppm. Under the 2025 composition the binder is N (13.07, 914.91 kg), labelled VOLATILITY-LIMITED. A conclusion the tree draws moves with a datum that has moved and is contested, so the grade is DATA-DEPENDENT and not STANDS. It is not WRONG: no refuting computation contradicts Lodders 2003.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: a settled CI N value above ~2400 ppm (e.g. from the forthcoming Lodders et al. 2025b 'Composition of CI-chondrites' or from Ryugu/Bennu bulk N), together with the tree citing the composition it actually uses. To NARROWED: if the tree used T_c quantitatively at a non-solar composition or pressure (it currently refuses to). To WRONG: only a demonstrated error in L03's computation at its stated hypotheses, and none was found.
